depiction.primary_object: clockwise circular arrow inside an outer ring
depiction.composition: centered circular glyph inside a circular border

ambiguity: Easy to confuse with bare refresh arrows, sync/loop icons, redo, or Creative Commons ShareAlike (though ShareAlike turns counterclockwise).

modifier_semantics.meaning: frames the arrow as a button or status badge

task_intents: renew an expiring subscription or license
rerun a failed build or job

Rerun failed nightly backup job for the NAS
Reset the garage keypad code before the cleaners come
Refresh expired OAuth token on the reporting script
Power cycle the cable modem and router in the closet
Trigger a full rebuild of the search index tonight
Do the winter set before November
Ask support to reprocess the stuck refund
Hard reset the smart thermostat so it finally pairs with the new Wi-Fi network
Rotate the canned goods in the pantry so the older tins are in front
Renew the domain registration for the family photo site before it lapses next Tuesday

near_misses.better: Creative Commons counterclockwise ShareAlike symbol or camera

near_misses.task: Take empty glass jars to the recycling bin
Pay the plumber for fixing the kitchen drain
Buy rechargeable AA batteries for the flash

reasoning: A clockwise circular arrow inside a circle universally reads as refresh, reload, restart, reset, or rotate. It is mainly an action or UI-control glyph rather than a concrete object, so it fits tasks where rebooting, resetting, rotating, or renewing is the core action, though most concrete tasks are better served by an icon of the object being reset or renewed.
